sentences.text: It is pertinent to note here that, the contesting defendants have denied and disputed relationship of late Smt. Lingamma with that of late Smt. Muniyamma and late Smt. Nanjamma.

Nanjamma.

It is further contended and deposed by D.W.1 that, plaintiffs are claiming partition through late Munishamappa and late Smt. Lingamma.

These Munishamappa and Smt. Lingamma are unknown to the family of defendants No.1 to 9.
14.

Muniyappa, Chikka Appaiah, Venkataramanappa and Narayanaswamy are children of Smt Muniyamma.

Parvathamma are children of Smt. Najamma.

15. On proper appreciation of pleadings of parties and evidence of P.W.1 and D.W.1, it is very much clear that, plaintiffs have claimed late Smt. Lingamma and late Smt. Muniyamma and late Smt.
Nanjamma are daughters of late Munishamappa.

On the other hand, contesting defendants have denied and disputed relationship of plaintiffs and late Smt. Lingamma with that of late Smt.
Muniyamma and late Smt. Nanjamma as well as relationship of plaintiffs and these defendants No.1 to 9.
The defendants have claimed late Smt. Nanjamma and late Smt. Muniyamma are not daughters of late Munishamappa.
On the other hand, they are daughters of late Venkatappa and late Smt. Gopamma.

16. When there is serious dispute with regard to relationship of parties, it is heavy burden on plaintiffs to prove relationship of late Smt. Lingamma with that of late Smt. Muniyamma and late Smt. Nanjamma as per Provision under Section 50 of Indian Evidence Act.
It is well settled proposition of law that, when relationship of one person with another person is in dispute in Civil suit, same has to be proved as per provisions of Sec. 50 of Indian Evidence Act.
Sec. 50 of Indian Evidence Act is an exception to General rule that, hearsay evidence is inadmissible and opinion based on such evidence.

As per Sec.50 of Evidence Act mere opinion expressed by conduct of a person, who is a member of a family or otherwise has special means of knowledge as to existence of relationship is admissible under this Section.
Such person need not be a member of family.
He may be an outsider.
It will suffice, if he has special means of knowledge.
So, a person watching conduct of members has to be treated as a person with special means of knowledge.
17. Further ingredients of Sec.50 of Evidence Act are as follows:- 1) There must be case, where court has to form an opinion as to the relationship of one person to another.
2) In such case, opinion expressed by conduct as to existence of such relationship is relevant fact.
3) But a person whose opinion is expressed by conduct is relevant must be person as member of family or otherwise has special means of knowledge on particular subject of relationship.

Late Nanjamma.

In this regard, reference has to be made to decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (1983) 3 SCC 118 in case of State of Bihar Vs. Radha Krishna Singh and others, wherein it is held that, in cases where the plaint genealogy is the very basis of plaintiffs case and since there is a tendency on the part of an interested person or a party in order to grab, establish or prove an alleged crime to concoct, fabricate or procure false genealogy to suit their ends, the court should endeavor to do justice on the materials and records uninfluenced and undaunted by any extraneous circumstances.

It is further held that, genealogies admitted or proved to be old and relied on in previous cases are doubtless relevant and in some cases may even be conclusive of the facts proved,
but there are several considerations which must be kept in mind viz.:
(a) Source of the genealogy and its dependability.
(b) Admissibility of the genealogy under the Evidence Act.
(c) A proper use in decisions or judgments on which reliance is placed.
(d) Age of genealogies.
(e) Litigation where such genealogies have been accepted or rejected.

On the question of admissibility the following tests must be adopted: (a) The genealogies of the families concerned must fall within the four-corners of Section 32(5) or Section 13 of the Evidence Act.
(b) They must not be hit by the doctrine of post litem motam.
(c) The genealogies or the claims cannot be proved by recitals, depositions or facts narrated in the judgment which have been held by a long course of decisions to be inadmissible.

(d) Where genealogy is proved by oral evidence, the said evidence must clearly show special means of knowledge disclosing the exact source, time and the circumstances under which the knowledge is acquired, and this must be clearly and conclusively proved.

20. Herein the case, if principles laid down in above decision are press into service to the facts and circumstances of case on hand, the contesting defendants have seriously disputed relationship of plaintiffs with that of deceased Smt. Late Muniyamma and Smt. Late Nanjamma as claimed in the plaint and also as mentioned in Ex.P1,
Now it is bounden duty of plaintiffs to prove their relationship with those persons by producing sufficient documentary and oral evidence before the court.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled proposition of law that, when relationship of one person with another person is in dispute in Civil suit, same has to be proved as per provisions of Sec. 50 of Indian Evidence Act.
Sec. 50 of Indian Evidence Act is an exception to General rule that, hearsay evidence is inadmissible and opinion based on such evidence.
As per Sec.50 of Evidence Act mere opinion expressed by conduct of a person, who is a member of a family or otherwise has special means of knowledge as to existence of relationship is admissible under this Section.
Such person need not be a member of family.
He may be an outsider.
It will suffice, if he has special means of knowledge.
So, a person watching conduct of members has to be treated as a person with special means of knowledge.
On the question of admissibility the following tests must be adopted: (a) The genealogies of the families concerned must fall within the four-corners of Section 32(5) or Section 13 of the Evidence Act.
(b) They must not be hit by the doctrine of post litem motam.
(c) The genealogies or the claims cannot be proved by recitals, depositions or facts narrated in the judgment which have been held by a long course of decisions to be inadmissible.
(d) Where genealogy is proved by oral evidence, the said evidence must clearly show special means of knowledge disclosing the exact source, time and the circumstances under which the knowledge is acquired, and this must be clearly and conclusively proved.
Now it is bounden duty of plaintiffs to prove their relationship with those persons by producing sufficient documentary and oral evidence before the court.
, plaintiffs cannot claim they are in joint possession and enjoyment of suit properties along with defendants No.1 to 9, 11 and 12.
